Global SEMIS - *Taiwan* - Our LATEST Thoughts + NEW Conclusions + INVESTOR Feedback + Our TOP PICKS 

There’s lots of very useful new work + new detail from Taiwan here below…

 

Sherman Shang’s Top Picks

  • TSMC
  • Mediatek
  • KYEC
  • ASE
  • C Sun

 

TSMC Capex Upside; Capacity Still Constrained

  • Sherman sees 2028 capex for TSMC now at $95-100bn
  • Samsung Foundry is also growing strongly off a high base

 

  • There are 20 front end fabs in the works for TSMC not including back end. Originally Sherman thought that number included back end factories. It doesn’t.

 

  • Sherman increased 2nm to 150K up from 120K after TSMC revised up capex. Demand still exceeds supply.
  • No change to 3nm 220K

 

 

  • Nvidia is half of all of A.I. wafer demand at TSMC

 

 

Datacentre Demand Is Over 30GW

  • TSMC says can it support 30GW of capacity but output 2026 is already 19GW and 2027 is 31GW.
  • That’s just for GPU and ASICs only rack and system the IT load is only 70-75% of power consumption. 40-45GW would be more reasonable for the whole system.

 

Intel AMD & ARM CPUS All Seeing Strong Growth

 

 

  • Intel rebound lifts CPU to 47.9m for the whole market. Intel is increasing but losing share according to Sherman.
  • AMD volumes are 10m for 2026 have booked volumes to 14m in 2027 that’s why AMD goes from 9% to 13% of TSMC sales.
  • Some investors think AMD can do 5-7 m Venice CPUs. Sherman thinks this is too high h’es at 3m.
  • Intel and AMD will increase prices 10-15% in September
  • AMD guidance is 60-70% which is doable on volumes and pricing
  • ARM based CPU is also increasing fast Vera CPUs are included in this

 

Intel EMIB Progressing Well

 

  • Intel EMIB chip capacity going from 10m WPM to 20m WPM to 40K wpm so even if substrate yields remain at 50% Intel can still pump out a lot of supply for Google V9 but it would have to take the yield hit.

 

HBM & Commodity Prices Peak in Q227 Based on ODM Checks

 

  • Based on conversations with ODM purchasing managers Sherman sees HBM prices declining slightly next year based on the LTAs memory companies have signed with key clients.
  • HBM supply is still tight but pricing will slightly decline peak is Q227 or Q327. Only going down a couple of percent per quarter
  • Memory vendors could push the price higher but they don’t want to do that they prefer to get a more sustainable LTA price is what ODMs are saying.

 

HBM Despec to 192GB Is Confirmed

 

  • The HBM despec is confirmed and reducses the BOM and implied ASP by 44%
  • Rubin Ultra despec 192GB 8 x 8hi. Down from 256GB and also down from Rubin which is 288GB.
  • Assuming 80% GM Rubin Ultra ASP is $45-46K not $75K making the chip and system cost a lot more appealing.
  • That means that the $1.5-2trn AI capex numbers based on the old specs of HBM should now be lower.

 

 

 

Networking Increases In Nvidia BOM Scale Up Scale Out & Copper

 

  • The BOM cost breakdown changes from GPU and memory to networking
  • Iin the future generations networking will be more than double for NVL288 and NVL586 and these are the designs Nvidia will try to focus clients on not NVL72
  • Rubin Ultra scales from GPU heavy to fabric heavy as systems scale the BOM cost from networking will more than double see p35. This is a combination of scale up and scale out
  • Interrack optical solution is scale up to connect the racks $4.6m 8% of the BOM $1.2m copper $3.5m optical.
  • Scale out $7.4m . 4 custom ASICs in 1 CPO switch and 64 optical engines.
  • Globally Lumentum is the best play on this

 

 

  • NVL72 Oberon is still the base case for Nvidia this year. But there is no upgrade in Rubin Ultra Oberon.
  • Nvidia has to push the concept of NVL576. By 2028 there wont be any more NVL72.
  • For NVL576 Nvidia adds a scale up optical layer but we don’t know if CPO or NPO.
  • NVL576 is scale out then between the racks its CPO or NPO and inside the racks its still copper.
  • The big debate is whether its CPO or NPO. NPO is easier to make the optical engine is outside the substrate. But CPO has the highest bandwidth.

 

CPO v NPO Debate Isnt About Costs Its About Yields

  • The Chinese all think its NPO that’s  what Innolight is saying but the Taiwanese think its CPO as NPO isn’t in the roadmap. All of the Taiwanese supply chain say this.
  • CPO are small volumes in 2027 and ramps in 2028 think CPO has the better opportunity in the coming years.
  • There is little difference in price between NPO and CPO its only $3K cheaper so  its not about the BOM cost.

 

 

  • TSMC moved from FOCI to other solutions as its yield is no good FOCI isn’t a good play on CPO anymore given its problems. TSMC isn’t happy with the low yields.
  • There are 4 other solutions. One of these is Corning working with Largan to be a more reliable source of CPO. The yield is better but not good enough. The yield rate is better than FOCI at the very least. Yields are around 50-60%% while FOCI was 30%. Nvidia needs the FAU assembly yield to be 70-80% before June 2027. They still have time to get the yields up.  Corning and Largan are more experienced in optical production.
  • Hon Hai is doing the racks but itds too early to talk about rack yields. Equipment players are positive on receiving more orders in Q4 but volumes are still limited. The rack schedule isn’t finalized and rack volumes are limited. We can infer this as Rubin Ultra volumes are revised down volumes should only be 1m for Ultra while Rubin units are going up.
  • For 2027 optical engine units should be 40m some are higher than this.
  • Insertion 1 Advantest is the key supplier its relatively simple

 

 

  • Insertion 2 is Teradyne and ficonTEC. They have related products for 3 and 4 but its more Hon Precision as they have more precision.

 

 

  • A lot of investors think Nvidia will cancel insertion 2 as testing time is too long. Sherman Shang doesn’t think that’s true insertion 2 is a must have.
  • The bottleneck is testing time is still 5 hours its way too long. TSMC needs its to 2-3 hours.
  • TSMC said its impossible to skip Insertion 2 despite what some think.

 

 

  • If we don’t get this fixed Nvidia may need to go to NPO

 

No Major Changes To COWOS Model

 

 

  • No changes to WPM. TSMC total COWOS 180K by end of 2027 and end of 2028 220K. Also COPOS 30K by end of 2028.
  • The only major change in the COWOS model recent ly is Sherman added in Open AI Jalapeno.
  • Jalapeno chip package size is 3-3.5” meaning 15-18 chips per COWOS wafer. TDP is 700 Watts.
  • 50K 2026 and 1.5m in 2027 is what Open AI talks about but based on Sherman’s COWOS numbers these isn’t enough capacity doesn’t look achievable in 2027

 

 

Nvidia Is Revising Down Rubin Ultra Revising Up Rubin 70% Easy to Beat

  • Nvidia revised down their Rubin Ultra volumes for 2027 from 1.5m to 1m based on current production plan and there could be some more downside due to delay the timing is very tight now. The chip is only being finalized now and the rack hasn’t been finalized yet it wont be until Q4.

 

 

  • But Rubin volumes are being revised up and Vera volumes are big in 2027. Rubin will remain the major product in 2027.
  • Nvidia 70% guidance should be easy to be including everything in the mix. COWOS capacity is growing 70%. Then add in networking revenues, Vera CPU and there is clear upside to those numbers.

 

 

MEDIATEK TOP PICK GAINING SHARE IN TPU.

  • Broadcom is 4m in 2026 and 7m in 2027 with a range of different projects: TPU is 5.6m. MTIA 464KK. META 930K.

 

 

  • For TPU of Mediatek and Broadcom combined the total in 2026 4.5m 2027 9.2m 2028 12-15m
  • But out of this Anthropic is 1m then 3.4m in 2027 and 5m in 2028 that’s a big swing factor.
  • AVGO for Google is 3.11 then 2.37m 2027 and 3.5m for 2028
  • Mediatek for Google is 500K 2026 3.54 2027 then 2028 4.5m
  • If GUC AMD or Alchip get involved its for the compute die not for the I/O die and production and COWOS so it wont impact Mediatek.
  • We haven’t seen Mediatek involved in V10 yet its still early stage
  • V8 ASP for Mediatek is $4K going to $15K for V9.

 

 

Sherman Thinks Expectations For AMD Venice Are Too High

  • Sherman is at 315K in 2026 and 2.5m for next year some are 5-7m this is too high. Its 1.3m total for 2026 and 3m for 2027.
  • META is a 36 chip rack solution. For others the 76 chip Helios design is late Q1 in terms of shipments.
  • But note AMD doesn’t sell racks it sells compute boards so it can still book these in CYQ4.

 

 

ASE TOP PICK STRONG MOMENTUM IN LEAP

  • LEAP has strong sales momentum. It includes FOCUS then TSMC OS and some testing but it doesn’t include CPO testing yet.
  • By the end of 2027 ASE & SPIL should have capacity of 50-60K.
  • ASE has 3 major FOCOS products Nvidia Vera, AMD Venue and Broadcom Tomahawk 6. All 3 of these are seeing very strong demand.

 

  • Tomahawk demand is huge in 2027 Accton has huge orders for this
  • Sherman is at US$8.4 bn compared to consensus at $7bn as all of his checks with equipment suppliers are seeing ASE very aggressive in orders.
  • TSMC only has 30-35K OS capacity the rest is ASE
  • ASE also has CPO testing with Teradyne testers it will be big in 2028 it could generate $2-3bn in sales.
  • ASE may announce expansion in the US even though IR says there is no plan for this, We hear the Chairman is considering it to follow TSMC’s into the US. They may need to raise capital to do this. Like TSMC it would be margin dilutive.

 

 

CSUN TOP PICK COPOS RAMP SHOULD DRIVE BIG ORDERS

  • COPOS new production lines should be 30K by the end of 2028
  • Equipment suppliers are C Sun Allring Grand Process Shibaura. Sherman likes C Sun the most.
  • OSAT expansion, AP localization, and AI-driven PCB demand point to a much stronger earnings trajectory than previously expected. TSMC’s CoWoS capacity is expected to increase from 70k wafers per month (wpm) by end-2025 to 120k/180k/220k wpm by the end of 2026/27/28; We estimate that each incremental 2-3k wpm of CoWoS capacity expansion could generate approximately US$2.5-3.0 million in revenue for C Sun.
  • C Sun’s content value will 2X as TSMC move to CoPoS from CoWoS. Domestic suppliers currently account for only around 10% of TSMC’s advanced packaging equipment spending, but we expect this ratio to rise to 15%/20%/30% in 2027/28/29, respectively, as TSMC deepens collaboration with local vendors to enhance supply chain responsiveness and process support.
  • ASE/SPIL/PTI) are all aggressively expanding. ASE/SPIL is expanding mostly OS process but also ASE’s full process. OSAT customers are expected to account for 25-30% of revenue in FY26, surpassing TSMC as C Sun’s largest revenue contributor, before rising further to 30-40% in FY27-28. The richer product mix and higher automation content should also support GM expansion.
  • 1H26 backlog reached NT$7.5-8.0b, roughly double YY, with advanced packaging accounting for 53% and advanced PCB 38% of backlog. AI-related applications now represent roughly 92% of backlog.
  • GM is forecast to rise from 43.3% in FY25 to 50.1%/51.8% in FY26/FY27 as higher-margin semiconductor equipment becomes a larger portion of sales.
  • CSun also supplies to Intel for EMIB T.

 

KYEC TOP PICK 2 NEW GROWTH DRIVERS

  • A lot of investors are still discussing Rubin testing time which is only up 20-30% which lower than expected. That’s why the stock hasn’t performed with Nvidia is the largest customer.
  • But in 2027 2 new growth drivers:
    • Mediatek is the second largest customer. There are 2 vendors ASE and KYEC tieh 50% share each. Before ASE used  burn in over from MCC but their deliveries are not on schedule due to some issue with the burn in equipment. About Us | Microprocessor Burn-In Test Systems | Micro Control Company So Mediatek is asking KYEC to have more burn in capacity. KYEC market share can increase to 70-80% form 50%. Mediatek is 18% of KYEC total sales in 2026 should go to 25-25% from smartphones and then smartphones.
    • TSMC Chip Probe outsourcing goes from NT$1.7bn will go to NT $10bn TSMC consigned 70 chip testers already by the end of 2025. That generated NT$1.7bn. This will make TSMC the third largest customer.
  • Ardentec 3264 TT is another company getting involved in testing for TSMC chip probe. It might be hard for Ardentec to source machines for Advantest
  • For testers all KYEC ASE and Ardentec all need to use the TSMC process its Advantest for testers and the probe card need to use Formfactor.

 

Advantest & Teradyne Orders from KYEC

  • TSMC will consign another 100 testers and asked KYEC to buy another 200 testers. These are all Advantest testers.
  • 1200 testers KYEC 200 are Teradyne Mellanox 1000 Advantest. Then 2027 2000 of which 300-400 for Mellanox the rest are for Advantest.

 

Hyperscaler Capex Should Continue Into 2028

  • Some investors commented that US hyperscalers capex spend is part of a political cycle. Google have told us they are able to write off most of their capex against a tax rebate. Without this their FCF would be much worse. US hyperscalers will continue to spend in 2027 and 2028 before any change in the presidency. As we go into 2028 the A.I. trade could become more political with it being a play on the Republicans remaining in charge
